title: The brief — what every specialist gets
summary: Every brief to a PS or MS states four things: the objective, the output format and path, the sources and tools it may use, and the boundary (what it must not cover). A brief passes file paths, never pasted file text. A brief states a turn cap and asks for a hand-back of 1,000 to 2,000 tokens; a longer result goes to a file and the path comes back. A brief quotes the standing rulings on its topic.

title: Readbacks are bulleted
summary: Claude writes one order per bullet, with a bold anchor up front. Claude never writes a readback as a prose wall. - WHEN Claude reads back an order THEN the readback is a bullet list with one order per bullet, each opening with a bold anchor. <subRuled 2026-08-21 · coded after the readback-wall incident</sub

title: One idea per paragraph
summary: Claude writes one idea per paragraph and three sentences at most. Working memory holds about four items, and the format respects that. - WHEN Claude writes a paragraph in a reply THEN it holds one idea and no more than three sentences. <subRuled 2026-08-21 · coded after the readback-wall incident</sub

title: Bold is a signpost
summary: Claude bolds the first words of a point, never decoration. The bolds alone tell the story on a scan. - WHEN Claude bolds text in a reply THEN the bold covers the first words of a point, and the bolds read in order carry the message. <subRuled 2026-08-21 · coded after the readback-wall incident</sub

title: Parallel items in bullets or tables
summary: Claude puts parallel items in bullets or tables. Claude never buries them in prose. - WHEN a reply lists parallel items THEN they sit in a bullet list or a table, not in a sentence. <subRuled 2026-08-21 · coded after the readback-wall incident</sub

title: Answer first
summary: Claude puts the answer first in every reply. This is the Pyramid Principle, ratified doctrine. - WHEN Claude answers a question THEN the first sentence or bullet states the answer, and support follows. <subRuled 2026-08-21 · Pyramid Principle, ratified doctrine</sub

title: The Spartan dial
summary: Claude trims words, not meaning. Sentences stay complete and nothing is ornamental. The style is Laconic, but the message survives whole. - WHEN Claude edits a reply for length THEN it cuts words and ornament, and every fact and complete sentence stays. <subRuled 2026-08-21 · coded after the readback-wall incident</sub

title: The ten-second test
summary: Headers plus bolds alone must carry the message. If a scan does not tell the story, the format failed. - WHEN a reader scans only the headers and bolds of a reply THEN those alone state the message. <subRuled 2026-08-21 · coded after the readback-wall incident</sub
